item.research_question: How do the strength, ductility, and fracture toughness of an equiatomic CrCoNi medium-entropy alloy compare to high-entropy alloys and conventional materials, particularly at cryogenic temperatures, and what mechanisms drive these properties?
item.processing_route: Arc-melted high-purity elements (>99.9%) under argon, drop-cast into copper moulds, homogenized at 1,200 °C for 24 h, cold-forged and cross-rolled to ~10 mm thickness (60% reduction), then annealed at 800 °C for 1 h in air to achieve a recrystallized microstructure with 5–50 μm grains.
item.test_conditions: Uniaxial tensile tests at 293 K, 198 K, and 77 K with a strain rate of 10⁻³ s⁻¹; Compact-tension (C(T)) fracture toughness tests at 293 K, 198 K, and 77 K with fatigue pre-cracking and side-grooving per ASTM E1820.
key_findings: At 77 K, yield strength reached 657 MPa and ultimate tensile strength reached 1,311 MPa, representing a ~50% increase from room temperature.
Tensile ductility (failure strain) increased to ~0.9 (90%) at 77 K, a ~25% increase from room temperature.
Fracture toughness (KJIc) at crack initiation increased from 208 MPa m1/2 at 293 K to 273 MPa m1/2 at 77 K.
Crack-growth toughness at 77 K reached critical stress-intensity values of ~430 MPa m1/2 (J ~900 kJ m⁻²).
The alloy exhibited a high strain-hardening exponent (n) of 0.4 at cryogenic temperatures.
The CrCoNi alloy showed ~15% higher tensile strength, ~30% higher ductility, and ~50% higher work of fracture than the five-component CrMnFeCoNi alloy at room temperature.
At 77 K, the CrCoNi alloy displayed ~25% higher KJIc, ~27% higher ductility, and ~31% higher work of fracture compared to the CrMnFeCoNi alloy.
item.mechanism: The exceptional damage tolerance results from continuous steady strain hardening that suppresses plastic instability, driven by pronounced dislocation activity and deformation-induced nano-twinning. Nano-twinning acts as a dominant deformation mode that provides a steady source of strain hardening, delaying necking and accommodating strain, with its intensity increasing as temperature decreases from room temperature to 77 K.
item.limitations: The yield strength at 77 K was slightly lower than the CrMnFeCoNi alloy, attributed to the non-uniform grain size of the current material; the volume fraction of void-initiating inclusions was not accurately quantified relative to the five-component alloy.
item.future_work: Further studies are needed to accurately determine the relative volume fractions of void-initiating inclusions in the MEA and HEA and to identify their chemistry and crystal structure by TEM after extraction from the voids.
quotes: strength, ductility and toughness of the CrCoNi alloy improve to strength levels above 1.3 GPa, failure strains up to 90% and KJIc values of 275 MPa m1/2.
nano-twinning contributes an important additional deformation mode that helps alleviate the deleterious effects of high strength that would normally be expected to result in lower toughness.

For a material with a tensile strength of 1.3 GPa to display ductilities (failure strains) of 90%, and 'valid' crack-growth fracture toughnesses that exceeds 430 MPa m1/2, all at liquid-nitrogen temperatures, is exceptional.
